title: Pharmacy First - Acute Sinusitis Pathway (6a/6b/6c/6d/6e/6f)
description: Shared acute sinusitis (rhinosinusitis) assessment with 6-route treatment selection: fluticasone, mometasone, phenoxymethylpenicillin, clarithromycin, doxycycline, erythromycin.

validations.message: Core symptom pattern should reflect one nasal symptom plus one additional sinusitis feature.
Antibiotic routes require >=2 bacterial sinusitis features plus persistent symptoms after 14-day high-dose intranasal steroid OR steroid unsuitable.
If bacterial criteria and antibiotic steroid-prerequisite are met, consider whether antibiotic route is more appropriate than intranasal steroid route.
6f erythromycin route requires age 16+, pregnancy/suspected pregnancy, and penicillin hypersensitivity.
6e doxycycline excludes pregnancy/suspected pregnancy and current breastfeeding.
6a fluticasone quantity should be 1 x 120-spray pack with minimum 112 actuations supplied.
6b mometasone quantity should be 1 x 18g spray with minimum 112 actuations supplied.
6e doxycycline quantity should match PGD-listed options.

common_sinusitis: Provide TARGET TYI-RTI leaflet and explain acute sinusitis is often viral and may take 2-3 weeks to resolve.
Self-care advice: paracetamol +/- ibuprofen if appropriate; supportive measures discussed.
Explain urgent red flags (orbital symptoms, visual changes, severe frontal headache, meningism signs, sepsis symptoms).
Advise to seek medical help if symptoms worsen rapidly/significantly or fail to improve as expected.
intranasal_steroids_6a_6b: Explain off-label use for sinusitis under national guidance and PGD.
Demonstrate/confirm nasal spray technique and adherence for full 14-day course.
Advise possible local adverse effects (epistaxis, throat irritation, altered taste/smell, headache).
Advise to seek advice for visual symptoms or persistent nosebleeds.
phenoxymethylpenicillin_6c: Take 500mg four times daily for 5 days and complete the course.
Take on an empty stomach (30 minutes before food or 2 hours after food).
Counsel on allergy signs and when to stop/seek urgent help.
Discuss anticoagulant monitoring/bleeding advice if relevant.
clarithromycin_6d: Take 500mg twice daily for 5 days and complete the course.
Can be taken with or without food.
Counsel on interaction risks (statins, anticoagulants, QT-risk drugs) and when to seek urgent advice.
Liquid may cause bitter aftertaste; practical advice given if suspension used.
doxycycline_6e: Day 1 take 200mg, then 100mg once daily for 4 more days.
Take with plenty of water; remain upright after taking to reduce oesophageal irritation risk.
Separate from antacids/iron/calcium/magnesium/zinc products by 2-3 hours.
Counsel on photosensitivity and to seek help for severe reactions.
erythromycin_6f: Take 500mg four times daily for 5 days and complete the course.
Take just before or with food.
Counsel on interaction/QT risk and when to seek urgent medical help.
If breastfeeding applies, discuss infant monitoring advice as relevant.

notes_for_implementation: This is a full dynamic-form module pattern matching the earlier long-form schemas (sections + branch blocks + route blockers + validations).
For production safety, use a dedicated interaction engine (BNF/SPC-backed) rather than UI checkbox blockers alone.
Keep an 'other exclusion / other interaction / clinical override rationale' free-text field with audit trail and clinician sign-off.
